_meta.title: Stays and rental cars: real costs by place

fieldKey.value: the figure, in the currency named
fieldKey.date: date of the figure or of publication
fieldKey.sourceType: primary-government | primary-company | primary-industry-data (STR/CoStar/tourism board) | industry-data-via-press | aggregator (Kayak, Hostelworld, AirDNA snippet) | secondary-press | secondary-blog
fieldKey.confirmed: true = read on the publisher's own page in this session; false = seen only in a search snippet, a secondary report, or a page that blocked direct fetch

_meta.method: Web search plus direct fetch of publisher pages where they allowed it. CoStar, AirDNA and several hertz.com pages returned 403 or rendered no content, so their figures come from search snippets or press restatements and are marked confirmed=false. Kayak 'average per day by car type' figures are live rolling aggregates of searches in the prior ~72 hours / recent period and move daily; they are aggregator data, not a company's published rate card. No rental company publishes a static per-class daily rate card; rates are dynamic and quote-only.
_meta.currencyNotes: Kayak .com pages report in USD even for YVR and MEX; the YYZ page summary claimed CAD but was fetched from kayak.com and is probably USD (flagged in uncertain). AirDNA public overview figures are shown in USD for every market, including London, Edinburgh, Dublin, Toronto, Vancouver and Mexico City.
_meta.spelling: American spelling in our own words; quoted names keep their original spelling.

roomTypesAndOccupancy.value: Industry convention, not law: standard king = 2 guests; standard double/queen-queen = up to 4; junior suite = 3-4 with sofa bed; one-bedroom suite = 4-6. Premier Inn and Travelodge family rooms take 2 adults + 2 children. Legal maximums come from fire codes per room, not a single published rule.

premierInn.value: Flex: free cancel until 1pm on arrival day; Semi-Flex: prepay, refundable until 3 full days before arrival; Advance: cheapest, least flexible (snippet says free cancel up to 28 days before, not verified)

marriott.value: Check-in 3pm-4pm, check-out 11am-12pm; Gold late check-out to 2pm on availability; Platinum+ guaranteed 4pm at most properties

travelodge.value: Check-in 3pm, check-out 12 noon; early check-in and late check-out sold as paid 'Extras' (price not published)

earlyLateFees.note: No chain publishes a fixed fee schedule; common practice is paid late checkout by the hour or a half-day rate. Nulled rather than guessed.

noShow.value: Guaranteed reservation not cancelled by deadline: first night's room and tax charged (flexible rates); prepaid/non-refundable rates forfeit the whole stay. Remaining nights are released.
noShow.publisher: Engine / hotel terms (e.g. Kimberly Hotel NYC terms)

US federal.value: FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees (16 CFR Part 464), effective 2025-05-12: short-term lodging and live-event tickets must show total price including mandatory fees (e.g. resort fees) more prominently than other pricing; government taxes may be excluded but disclosed.

New York City.value: DCWP rule effective 2026-02-21: total price incl. all mandatory fees up front; mandatory card holds/deposits must be disclosed. Penalties $525 / $1,050 / $3,500 (per Herrick law firm summary).

United Kingdom.value: DMCC Act 2024 consumer provisions effective 2025-04-06: mandatory charges (incl. resort fees and local taxes payable on arrival) must be in headline price.

Canada.value: Competition Act drip-pricing amendment in force 2022-06-23: advertised price must include all mandatory non-government fees (incl. resort/facility fees); GST/PST/MRDT may be excluded.

acriss.note: Letter positions and letters were confirmed from the ACRISS page; the long names for some less-common letters (N, H, J, R, G, U, W, O and some type/fuel names) are the long-standing ACRISS meanings, filled from knowledge and not all quoted on the fetched page.

averageDailyByAirport._note: Kayak rolling averages by Kayak's own coarse classes (small ~ ACRISS M/E/C, medium ~ I/S, large ~ F, SUV ~ xFxx). Aggregator, not rate card. Retrieved 2026-09-30.

MEX (Mexico City).note: Mexican online base rates exclude the legally mandatory third-party liability cover sold at the counter, which commonly multiplies the real daily cost several times. Treat as bait price, not real cost.

enterprisePolicy.value: Some one-way rentals carry a one-time drop charge or a per-mile/km charge on top of the rate; varies by pickup, return and other factors; even same-city returns can incur it; disclosed at booking and payable at pickup. Unlimited mileage on one-ways for most classes except large passenger vans, cargo vans, large SUVs, exotics.

exampleJFKtoDC.note: One-day Enterprise one-way JFK to Washington DC: $94 drop fee on a ~$60 base rate

hertzOneWay.value: Commonly priced into the rate or as per-mile charges on some rates ($0.25-$0.29/mile reported on corporate/one-way rates over 200 miles); Hertz return-location change fee $12.99 applies to modifications

avisOneWay.value: Often $0 separate drop fee in the US with cost folded into the daily rate; drop charge may apply on some rates

crossBorderOneWay.value: Budget: no one-way rentals into Mexico; car must return to US. Enterprise UK/IE: separate fees for one-way and cross-border hires (amounts not published).

enterpriseUS.value: Unlimited on most US classes; limited on large passenger vans, cargo vans, large SUVs, exotics; overage $0.10-$0.25 per mile/km; no restriction for out-of-state or driving to Canada

enterpriseEU.value: Unless 'Unlimited mileage' appears on the Summary, a charge per extra mile/km above the allowance shown

hertzCanada.value: Unlimited mileage stated as standard for Hertz Canada rentals via tour-operator terms; limited plans exist on some rates. Separate reports of '200 km/day' caps not confirmed.

hertzUS.value: 29-minute grace; from the 30th minute, extra hours charged (reported at 1/5 of the daily rate per hour, capped so that after ~5 hours a full extra day applies); optional coverages charged a full day with no grace
hertzUS.publisher: Hertz (terms page returned HTTP 500; wording via AutoSlash/UponArriving)

enterpriseUS.value: 29-minute grace for daily rentals; returned within 2.5 hours of pickup time on a later day = hourly charges (rate on contract); 2.5 hours or more = an extra day; after-hours returns stay renter's responsibility until next-business-day check-in

enterpriseUK.value: 29-minute grace for daily hires; outside it, daily hire charges payable

enterpriseEUSchedule.value: Excess time charged per full or partial hour/day beyond 1; hourly charges never exceed the cost of 1 extra day; returning out of hours or to another location keeps time & distance running until check-in

value.fuelPurchaseOption: full tank prepaid at about local pump price minus $0.15/gal (Canada: minus 5 cents/L); no refund for unused fuel
value.refuelingServiceCharge: about $9.49 per gallon reported for 2026 (older program: pump price plus $6.99 flat)

enterpriseUS.value: Full-to-full; else refueled at a local Enterprise per-gallon rate 'typically above the local pump price'; Pre-pay fuel sold only as full tanks at local price minus a per-gallon discount, non-refundable

enterpriseUKIE.value: If Fuel Service Option not bought and car returned short: fuel charge at the Summary rate x missing eighths (gauge rounded to nearest 1/8 or telematics) + a location-set refueling fee (UK reported 'up to £15'); no credit for extra fuel. EVs: kWh shortfall x market price + admin fee.

hertzUS.note: Spouse/civil-union partner 25+ added free in California and Iowa (state law) or for Gold Plus Rewards members; AAA and USAA members get free additional drivers
Minimum age 20 in most states; 18 in NY and MI; 19 in AL and NE. Fee waived for AAA members 20-24.

enterpriseUK.note: Enterprise UK rents to 25+ on standard classes; under-25s steered to Enterprise Car Club (19+). Surcharge amount not published.

damageExcessUKIE.value: Enterprise UK Damage Waiver excess roughly £1,750-£2,700 per incident by class, reduced to £100-£250 with Excess Protection; Ireland roughly €2,000-€3,000 reduced to €0-€500 (table layout garbled in extraction; class-to-amount mapping uncertain)

extensions.value: Extensions priced at the current rate for added days, not the booked rate; Enterprise EU schedule reserves the right to recalculate the whole rental at actual duration, which can raise charges; prepaid rates usually cannot be extended at the prepaid price

USToCanada.value: Enterprise: most US rentals may be driven to Canada with no special permit or fee and no mileage restriction; tell the counter and get a Canadian Non-Resident Insurance Card. Budget has a similar published US-Canada FAQ.

enterprise.value: Vehicles rented from Enterprise in the United States cannot be driven into Mexico.

budget.value: Allowed only on corporate accounts, US-resident renters, car must return to the US (no one-way into Mexico); Mexican Automobile Liability Insurance required, sold only at counters in Texas, Arizona and California

mexicoLaw.value: Third-party liability insurance is mandatory for all vehicles in Mexico; US policies and credit-card coverage generally not accepted. Enterprise Mexico requires Third Party Liability Protection unless proof of Mexico-valid liability cover.

MexicoToUS.value: Enterprise Mexico permits US crossing only from Tijuana, Mexicali, Hermosillo, Monterrey and Saltillo; Mexico City rentals may not cross

UKIreland.value: Enterprise charges separate cross-border fees (UK to Ireland / Northern Ireland to Republic); amounts not published

uncertain: Mexico City ISH: the brief said 5%; the Codigo Fiscal sets 3.5% for hotels, hostels and motels and 5% only for homes/apartments booked through platforms. Model both.
Toronto MAT: the brief's 6% is right as of 2026-08-01; it was 8.5% from 2025-06-01 to 2026-07-31. Stays in that window used 8.5%.
Los Angeles TMD is 2.0% for hotels with 50+ rooms (not 1.5%); smaller hotels likely 1.5% or exempt, not confirmed. Measure TT failed, so TOT stays 14%.
Vancouver effective tax: whether GST cascades on PST+MRDT+MEMRDT in practice for every provider was read from a BC notice summary, not the notice itself.
CoStar, AirDNA and most hertz.com pages blocked direct fetch (403/500/empty JS); their numbers are from search snippets or press restatements.
AirDNA ADRs are shown in USD for non-US markets; convert at the date's rate. AirDNA's Mexico City 'monthly revenue $11,939' looks like MXN or an error and was not used.
Kayak YYZ averages: summary said CAD but the page was kayak.com (normally USD). Treat currency as unknown until re-read on kayak.ca.
Kayak averages are rolling and date-dependent; MEX base rates exclude mandatory liability insurance and badly understate real cost.
Hertz young renter fee amounts ($19-$25 typical, NY $25-$35) come from secondary sites; Hertz's own pages confirm only that the fee exists and the minimum ages.
Hertz late-return hourly = 1/5 of daily rate is a secondary report; Hertz confirms the 29-minute grace in forum-quoted terms only.
Hertz US refueling charge ~$9.49/gal for 2026 is from a third-party tips site.
Enterprise UK/IE damage excess class mapping was garbled by PDF extraction.
Edinburgh £220 ADR (12 months to May 2025) has unclear attribution.
Cancun ADR $116 (2025) seems low for the market and may be a room-only subset.
Mexico City hotel ADR only available as a November 2024 figure (1,600 MXN) from a brokerage note; no official 2025 ADR found.
Toronto full-year 2025 ADR not found; only October (CAD 294.90) and November (CAD 274.79) 2025.
Hotel parking outside NYC, early check-in/late check-out fees, and room occupancy limits have no published primary figures; left null or described as convention.
London Congestion Charge 2026 figure mentioned in a parking note was not verified this session.
Palm Springs vacation-rental ADR $476 is from an AirROI-type aggregator; Visit Greater Palm Springs monthly figures ($720 April 2025, $385 May 2025) vary sharply by season.
